questions.question: When was the national anthem adopted in its Hindi version?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The national anthem of India is **Jana Gana Mana**.
 
• It was adopted in its Hindi version by the Constituent Assembly as the** National Anthem of India on 24 January 1950.**__
 
• It was originally composed in Bengali by poet Rabindranath Tagore as Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata.
 
• It was first publicly sung on 27 December 1911 at the Calcutta (now Kolkata) Session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• It was translated in Hindi by Captain Abid Ali and composed by Captain Ram Singh.

questions.question: What combination of paternal chromosome results in a female?
questions.solution:
__**XX ​combination of paternal chromosome results in a female.**__

 
• Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes. Out of these 23 pairs, 22 pairs are autosomes and only one pair is the ‘Sex Chromosome’.
 
• Both males and females carry two sets of sex chromosomes.
 
• Male has XY sex chromosome in which both are active.
 
• Female has XX sex chromosome in which one is active.
 
• All children inherit an X chromosome from their mother. Thus, the sex of the children will be determined by the type of chromosome inherited from their father whether X or Y.
 
• A child who inherits the Y chromosome will be a male and who inherits the X chromosome will be a female.

questions.question: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon is associated to which of the following ancient cultures?
questions.solution:
__

• It was among Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
 
• It was described as an interesting feat of engineering with an ascending series of tiered gardens containing a wide range of trees, shrubs, and vines, resembling a large green mountain constructed of mud bricks.
 
• It was said to have been built in the ancient city of Babylon in Iraq.
 
• Mesopotamia, a historical region of Western Asia situated along the Tigris–Euphrates river system.

questions.question: In which year the National Food Security Act was passed in India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **National food security act was passed on 10th September 2013.__**

**Key features:**

 
• The Act covers up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population subsidized foodgrains under the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS).
 
• The eligible persons will be entitled to receive 5 Kgs of foodgrains per person per month at subsidized prices of Rs. 3 for rice, Rs. 2 for wheat and, Rs.1 for coarse grains.
 
• According to the existing Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), households will continue to receive 35 Kgs of foodgrai
ns per household per month.
 
• The Act also has a special focus on nutritional support for women and children.
 
• Besides food to pregnant women and lactating mothers during pregnancy and six months after childbirth, they will also be entitled to receive maternity benefit of Rs. 6,000.
 
• Children upto 14 years of age will be entitled to nutritious meals as per the prescribed nutritional standards.

questions.question: Which of the following synthetic chemical is responsible for ozone layer depletion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorofluorocarbons**__.

__
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons(CFC)**__** are responsible for ozone layer depletion.**
 
• Ozone gas is continuously formed by the action of UV rays on molecular oxygen and also degraded into molecular oxygen in the stratosphere.
 
• CFC has disrupted this balance and increase the degradation of Ozone gas which is called __**Ozone depletion**__.
 
• Although ozone depletion is occurring in the stratosphere, the depletion is especially marked over the Antarctic region. This has resulted in the formation of a large area of the thinned ozone layer, commonly called the **ozone hole**
 
• The adoption of the** Montreal Protocol in 1987 bans the production of CFCs, halons and other ozone-depleting chemicals.**

**Chemical Equation**

CFCl₃ + UV Light ==> CFCl₂ + Cl

Cl + O₃ ==> ClO + O₂

ClO + O ==> Cl + O₂

The free chlorine atom is then free to attack another ozone molecule

Cl + O₃ ==> ClO + O₂

ClO + O ==> Cl + O₂

and again ...

Cl + O₃ ==> ClO + O₂

ClO + O ==> Cl + O₂

and again... for thousands of times

questions.question: Which of the following gas causes rancidity in food product?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Oxygen gas causes rancidity in food products is also called oxidative rancidity.**__
 
• Rancidity refers to the spoilage of food in such a way that it becomes undesirable (and usually unsafe) for consumption.
 
• Oils and fats can be especially susceptible to rancidity because their chemistry can make them exceptionally susceptible to oxygen damage.
 
• During the oxidative rancidity, oxygen molecules interact with the structure of the oil and damage its natural structure in a way that can change its taste, its smell, and its safety for consumption.
 
• Oxidative rancidity can be prevented by light-proof and airtight packaging and also by the addition of antioxidants.

questions.question: Which state in India has made roof top rainwater harvesting structure compulsory to all the houses in the state?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__ is the first state in India that has made rooftop rainwater harvesting structures compulsory to any or all the homes within the state.
 
• This scheme was launched in 2001 and has been implementing in all rural areas of Tamil Nadu.
 
• In Rainwater, harvesting raindrops are collected and stored for future use in a deep pit (well, shaft, or borehole), aquifer, a reservoir with percolation, instead of allowing them to run off. 
 
• It provides water for gardens, livestock, irrigation, domestic use with proper treatment, indoor heating for houses, etc.
